summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted for worsening rectal prolapse with associated fecal incontinence, rectal bleeding, and recent weight gain. She underwent a perineal rectosigmoidectomy with levatorplasty the following day. Post-operatively, she developed a transient post-operative ileus with abdominal distension, managed conservatively without a nasogastric tube. She had low urine output initially, which resolved with IV fluids and restart of home diuretics. A urinalysis before discharge revealed a urinary tract infection, and she was started on ciprofloxacin. Her diet was advanced as bowel function returned, and she passed a bowel movement on hospital day 6. She recovered well, with stable chronic diastolic heart failure and no surgical complications. She was discharged home with services on day 8 with instructions for bowel management, activity restrictions, and follow-up.
